headline: Software Engineer Asks For Pay Cut To Stay Below EPFO Wage Ceiling And Avoid 'Adulting Responsibilities'
body:
Q: Rajesh, you’ve been working at the same junior developer salary for six years now. Why did you explicitly turn down this month’s hike, which would have put your monthly earnings just above the new ₹25,000 EPFO ceiling?

A: Look, as long as I’m under that ceiling, the government and the HR department handle my future like a gentle parent. Once you cross that threshold, suddenly you’re expected to have opinions on tax brackets, investment portfolios, and where your money goes. I’m not ready for that level of consciousness.

Q: But you’re currently living in a shared PG where the bathroom door doesn't lock and you pay your rent in installments. Don't you want a higher salary to improve your quality of life?

A: It’s a trade-off. If I take the raise, I become a 'high-earner' who has to worry about inflation-adjusted returns and retirement planning. Staying under the ceiling means I can pretend the financial system is a magical machine I don't need to understand. My plan is to stay exactly at ₹24,999 until I turn sixty-five, at which point I’ll retire with a collective shrug from the payroll office.

Q: Does your manager understand this logic, or do they think you've finally lost it?

A: My manager thinks I’m a martyr for corporate simplicity. He’s actually asked me to teach a workshop next week titled 'Maintaining Mediocrity in a High-Growth Economy.' It’s going to be very liberating to earn less while everyone else stresses over their provident fund percentages.
caption: Why strive for a raise when you can just embrace the sweet, simple bliss of staying under the ceiling? 📈📉 #EPFO #CorporateLife #SalaryHike #FinanceHumor (satire)
igHook: Would you actually take a pay cut just to avoid dealing with tax forms?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a beige office cubicle desk with a single dusty calculator and a stack of confusing financial forms, with a blurred employee looking out a window.
